questions.question: Why is the model registry stored inside the modelwise skill folder instead of at the repository root?
questions.answer: Plugin installers copy only the plugin's own folder; files outside it break after install. A self-contained skill folder also works as a ZIP upload.
key_points: installers copy only the plugin folder

questions.question: Why are the registry files JSON rather than YAML?
questions.answer: Python's standard library reads JSON everywhere; YAML needs PyYAML and tomllib needs Python 3.11+, so JSON keeps zero install steps.

questions.question: What does the 'balanced' priority pick, and what earlier approach did it replace and why?
questions.answer: The cheapest model whose fit clears the quality bar with one point of headroom; it replaced a log-cost penalty that picked Haiku for moderate feature builds (too weak).
key_points: penalty picked a too-weak model (Haiku) for moderate builds

questions.question: Why don't the SKILL.md files pin a model and effort in their frontmatter?
questions.answer: claude.ai skill upload rejects unknown frontmatter keys, so portability won; defaults went into metadata and the skill text.

questions.question: What happens when someone asks modelwise for a video, and why?
questions.answer: No generator is recommended: OpenAI shut down the Sora 2 API (2026-09-24) and Anthropic doesn't generate video. It routes the prompt-writing to a text model and still writes the full video prompt.
key_points: fallback to text model to write the prompt

questions.question: Why was the single audio task split into three?
questions.answer: One audio task mixed transcription, speech and voice agents and produced nonsensical picks; splitting gave each its right model.

questions.question: How is the registry kept current and checked?
questions.answer: A weekly watcher checks vendor model pages and opens an issue for unknown IDs; a human updates the card from official docs, runs validate.py --fix (regenerates the routing table) and CI runs validation and router tests.

questions.question: What assumption about OpenAI's lineup turned out to be wrong, and how was it caught?
questions.answer: The plan assumed GPT-5.x was current; a research agent told not to trust memory found GPT-6 (Astra/Sol/Luna) is current and Sora/DALL-E were shut down.

questions.question: Google releases a new video model. What do you change in the repo?
questions.answer: Add google to the provider enum, an effort mapping and a prompt-style guide, a model card with video_out and fit for video.generate, a watcher source; run validate --fix and tests. The video fallback stops applying automatically.

questions.question: Why does routing use a Python script plus a generated ROUTING_TABLE.md instead of letting the model pick from the cards?
questions.answer: Deterministic and testable — same inputs give the same answer regardless of the running model — and the table covers environments that can't run scripts (e.g. ChatGPT Projects).
